strengths: Virginia DWR publishes exact public boating accesses and coordinates.
Virginia DWR publishes segmented float guides with distances, hazards, and gauge references.
The Maury guide supplies an explicit low-water condition tied to USGS 02024000.
Virginia extends the existing Appalachian coverage without duplicating the separate West Virginia work.
risks: Private banks require explicit no-trespass caveats outside public accesses.
Broken dams, cold water, and whitewater difficulty require route-specific safety treatment.

strengths: North Carolina manages 250 free boating access areas on more than 100 water bodies.
The state recognizes multiple long paddle trails including the Roanoke, Dan, Yadkin, Haw, and Deep rivers.
The Roanoke trail publishes designated access spacing and segment managers.
risks: Many route details are delegated to partner organizations, increasing source joins.
Dam releases and lowland threshold guidance require corridor-by-corridor verification.

strengths: Colorado has the deepest active USGS discharge network in the shortlist.
The Arkansas Headwaters corridor provides six official sections and more than 25 developed river accesses.
The Upper Colorado provides developed BLM access and camping.
risks: A high share of obvious corridors are technical whitewater with seasonal and cold-water risk.
Private access, drought closures, and release-sensitive conditions raise evidence cost.

strengths: New York publishes more than 500 public boating access sites.
The state identifies extensive river and flatwater paddling opportunities and a 50-launch Susquehanna trail project.
The active USGS discharge network is broad.
risks: The statewide launch directory is less route-segmented than the Virginia and North Carolina sources.
A large share of official access inventory is lake, canal, or coastal rather than scored moving-water routes.

selectionReason: Virginia has the strongest immediately publishable evidence chain: exact state-managed endpoints, route segmentation, supported gauges, explicit threshold guidance on the leading corridor, and manageable geographic continuity.
